stages.title: Close the Post-Core Traceability Release Gate
stages.access_decision: Narrow after preflight; no broader generic access
stages.finding: Cross-layer traceability work can justify several modules, but three whole source layers plus all tests permit unrelated changes. Add docs/adr/** only when the pre-change report proves an ADR is required.

stages.title: Post-Core Traceability Corrective Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Product read-only is strong, but the prompt orders the agent to create docs/audits files and commit while the roadmap grants no write paths and a read-only sandbox. Make the agent return a report payload and let the controller write/commit, or grant only the exact report and index paths.

stages.title: Define and Govern the Narrow Pilot Scope
stages.access_decision: Keep; narrow tests where practical
stages.finding: The named domain files and governed documentation fit pilot-scope decisions. Runtime activation remains approval-sensitive. No broader write access is justified.

stages.title: Select and Govern the Production Application Stack
stages.access_decision: Keep docs-only
stages.finding: This is a decision gate and correctly excludes implementation code. ADR/current/log/runbook access is appropriate.

stages.title: Bootstrap the Production Application Shell and Engineering Baseline
stages.access_decision: Narrow CI, scripts, config, and source paths
stages.finding: src/**, scripts/**, config/**, and .github/** allow broad code, workflow, and supply-chain changes. Restrict to the approved composition root, health/config modules, validation scripts, and exact CI workflow files.

stages.title: MVP Scope and Architecture Decision Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Same read-only-versus-report-write/commit contradiction as Stage 002.

stages.title: Design and Implement the Durable Database Schema and Migrations
stages.access_decision: Narrow persistence modules; allow exact migration config if needed
stages.finding: The stage may need a selected migration-tool config file not listed. Whole domain and infrastructure globs are broader than schema/mapping work requires. Bind paths to the approved Stage 004 stack.

stages.title: Implement Durable Repositories and Transaction Boundaries
stages.access_decision: Narrow to repositories, UoW, transaction adapters, and exact migrations
stages.finding: Whole application/domain/infrastructure trees exceed the repository/transaction scope. Add docs/schema/** only if this stage legitimately changes the approved schema.

stages.title: Implement Immutable Artifact Storage, Outbox, Workers, and Crash Recovery
stages.access_decision: Narrow to artifact, outbox, worker, and reconciliation modules
stages.finding: config/** and whole application/domain/infrastructure trees are too broad. Permit one exact reconciliation command location if the repository convention requires it.

stages.title: Durable Platform and Persistence Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Same audit-control contradiction; validation also needs persistence, migration, and concurrency profiles beyond the single unit command.

stages.title: Implement Authentication, Session Security, and AccessContext Construction
stages.access_decision: Strongly narrow auth/session/middleware paths
stages.finding: An authentication stage with src/** and config/** can alter unrelated authorization, domain, notification, or deployment behavior. Limit it to verified-claim middleware, AccessContext, session/auth adapters, config/auth/**, exact migrations, and security tests.

stages.title: Implement Customer Account Lifecycle, Versioned Configuration, and Onboarding API
stages.access_decision: Narrow customer modules; add exact API-contract and ADR paths
stages.finding: Versioned request/response contracts are required, but openapi/** or the approved transport-contract path is absent. docs/adr/** may be needed for retention/anonymization decisions.

stages.title: Identity, Authorization, and Customer-Isolation Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Read-only is appropriate, but report creation and commit ownership must be made controller-only and machine-verifiable.

stages.title: Select and Approve the First Tucson or Pima County Production Source
stages.access_decision: Keep write scope; add network read policy and exact registry tests
stages.finding: Write access is narrow, but source comparison can involve live external access. Enforce destination allowlists, read-only HTTP methods, response-size limits, and no credentials. The single named test file may be under-inclusive.

stages.title: Implement Durable Scheduled Acquisition and the Approved Live Connector
stages.access_decision: Add exact scheduler/worker and manual-replay paths; narrow everything else
stages.finding: The task includes scheduling, leases, and manual reprocessing, but only acquisition-specific files are allowed. This may force code into the wrong layer unless exact existing worker/command modules are added.

stages.title: Implement the Production Source Parser, Replay, and Backfill Contract
stages.access_decision: Keep; add schema docs only if contract changes
stages.finding: The source-specific parser paths are focused and replay/backfill remains bounded. New dependencies should require a separate approved path change.

stages.title: Implement Required Production Geography and Address Resolution
stages.access_decision: Add docs/schema/** and only an approved provider-adapter path
stages.finding: Geography provenance can change schema documentation. If an external geocoder is approved, the exact adapter/transport path should be added rather than widening infrastructure generally.

stages.title: Pilot Source, Ingestion, Normalization, and Geography Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Read-only safety is good; report write/commit and complete source/geography validation remain unresolved.

stages.title: Implement the Authorized Customer API and Query Projections
stages.access_decision: Add the exact API transport/router path; narrow application/infrastructure
stages.finding: The prompt must expose endpoints, but the roadmap omits the transport layer created by Stage 005 unless it happens to live under infrastructure. This can force architecture leakage or make completion impossible.

stages.title: Build the Authenticated Frontend Foundation and Onboarding Experience
stages.access_decision: Keep frontend subtree, permit only the selected package manager and exact config files
stages.finding: All major lockfiles are writable and validation contains no frontend lint/type/build/test command. Dependency and package-script execution need supply-chain controls.

stages.title: Build the Explainable Opportunity Dashboard and Lead Workflow
stages.access_decision: Keep frontend scope; make dependency files read-only unless explicitly needed
stages.finding: Dashboard work is focused, but broad tests and writable package/lock files allow unrelated dependency changes. The roadmap lacks browser, accessibility, build, and end-to-end validation.

stages.title: Customer API, Frontend, and Data-Exposure Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Data-exposure auditing is correctly read-only, but the controller/report contract and full API/UI security test profile must be explicit.

stages.title: Implement Email Notification Orchestration and Delivery
stages.access_decision: Require provider approval file; add exact webhook route; narrow notification modules
stages.finding: Email introduces customer data, external delivery, reputation, webhooks, and cost, yet no machine-enforced provider approval exists. The transport path for verified webhooks is also absent.

stages.title: Email Delivery Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: The dedicated audit is valuable, but its immutable report and commit must be controller-owned and provider evidence must be authenticated.

stages.title: Implement Controlled SMS Infrastructure Behind a Disabled Feature Flag
stages.access_decision: Require provider approval and immutable disabled-by-default enforcement
stages.finding: SMS has legal/consent/cost exposure. The prompt says approval is required, but the roadmap has no approval file. Add an exact webhook route and CI policy proving production enrollment/sending cannot be enabled in this stage.

stages.title: Build Internal Review and Source Operations Tooling
stages.access_decision: Narrow privileged operations and add exact internal transport/domain paths
stages.finding: This stage creates highly privileged review, reprocessing, merge, source-disable, and retry capabilities. Broad app/infra access plus no explicit internal API route and domain paths creates cross-tenant and evidence-destruction risk.

stages.title: Notification, SMS, and Operations Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit materialization contract
stages.finding: Audit separation is good; controller-only report materialization and complete notification/operations validation are required.

stages.title: Implement the Privacy-Conscious Analytics Event Model
stages.access_decision: Narrow to analytics-event modules and registry
stages.finding: Whole domain/application/infrastructure access is unnecessary for server-side event emission and increases privacy risk. External analytics integration should require its own approval artifact.

stages.title: Implement Observability, Health, Alerting, and Operational Runbooks
stages.access_decision: Narrow to instrumentation middleware, health, alert rules, and runbooks
stages.finding: src/** and ops/** are excessively broad for observability. A mistake can leak PII/secrets into logs, expose health internals, or create unbounded metric cardinality and cost.

stages.title: Implement Backup, Restore, Reconciliation, and Rollback Procedures
stages.access_decision: Remove migration write access by default; separate authoring from destructive recovery execution
stages.finding: Backup/restore code is inherently dangerous. src/**, ops/**, and migrations/** permit unrelated or destructive changes. Recovery execution needs a separate approval and environment capability gate.

stages.title: Perform Security, Privacy, Performance, and Recovery Hardening
stages.access_decision: Redesign as read-only audit plus per-finding correction stages
stages.finding: This mega-stage can modify almost the whole repository, dependencies, deployment, configuration, migrations, tests, and workflows. It defeats narrow-stage governance and can hide control weakening inside a hardening commit.

stages.title: Formal Pilot Release Test Matrix and Release Gate Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit contract and encode the full release matrix
stages.finding: The read-only gate is conceptually strong, but the roadmap runs only Python unittest despite requiring frontend, E2E, migration, security, performance, restore, and rollback evidence.

stages.title: Prepare and Execute the Controlled Staging Deployment
stages.access_decision: Add staging account/environment capability manifest and plan/apply split
stages.finding: Filesystem paths are focused, but they do not constrain cloud, DNS, email sandbox, database, or secret side effects. Pin the staging account, region, resource set, commit, and approved actions.

stages.title: Final Staging and Pilot Readiness Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit contract and verify immutable staging evidence
stages.finding: The readiness audit is safe only if staging evidence is signed, environment-bound, and controller materialization is explicit.

stages.title: Deploy the Controlled Production Pilot
stages.access_decision: Require two-person production approval, target pinning, plan/apply split, and canary
stages.finding: Production deployment can migrate data, change providers, enable schedules, and enroll users. Path controls cannot prevent wrong-account deployment, duplicate alerts, or destructive changes.

stages.title: Production Pilot Launch Verification Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit contract and authenticate production evidence
stages.finding: Read-only verification is appropriate, but production facts must come from trusted, signed deployment/monitoring evidence rather than self-reported agent output.

stages.title: Implement Pilot Feedback and Business Validation Workflow
stages.access_decision: Narrow feedback modules; add exact API/OpenAPI path and retention approval
stages.finding: The stage spans all backend layers, frontend, migrations, and analytics. The transport path is missing, and optional free text/customer outcomes create privacy and cross-customer risks.

stages.title: Pilot Feedback and Business Validation Audit
stages.access_decision: Fix audit contract and bind the approved review snapshot
stages.finding: The final audit is read-only, but the approval snapshot, evidence, report, and audited commit need cryptographic binding and controller-only materialization.

appendices.title: Audit Correction Prompt
appendices.access_decision: Disable until prompt exists and derive a per-finding allowlist
appendices.finding: Appendix A is included in normal execution, requires no explicit invocation or approval, has no hard lock, and can change nearly the entire repository including deploy and CI. Its prompt file is absent from the supplied prompt pack, so its behavior cannot be cross-checked.

appendices.title: Optional Controlled SMS Canary Enablement Prompt
appendices.access_decision: Keep disabled; enable hard lock and exact canary capability scope
appendices.finding: Approvals and explicit invocation are present, but the hard lock is disabled by default, the prompt is absent from the pack, and write access is broad across backend/frontend/migrations/dependencies. Activation must be cohort/window/provider/account bound.

appendices.title: Optional Controlled SMS Canary Activation Audit
appendices.access_decision: Keep read-only; supply and verify the missing prompt
appendices.finding: Read-only scope is appropriate, but the referenced prompt is absent and the same report-write/commit ambiguity applies.
